xref.title: Drowning Accident (1983)
xref.body: Dennis Wilson, a member of The Beach Boys, tragically drowned in a diving accident in 1983. He left behind an unfinished recording titled "Holy Man," which Taylor Hawkins later completed in 2019 with the help of Roger Taylor and Brian May. "Wilson drowned in a diving accident back in 1983."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Taylor Hawkins and the Co-Tale Riders (2006)
xref.body: In 2006, Taylor Hawkins formed his own band, Taylor Hawkins and the Co-Tale Riders, a name reflecting his sense of humor and humbleness. The band featured crack session musicians and released three albums, collaborating with figures like Roger Taylor and Brian May (Queen), Nancy Wilson (Heart), Joe Walsh (Eagles), Chrissie Hynde (Pretenders), and LeAnn Rimes. "The first came in 2006 when he formed a band called Taylor Hawkins and the Co-Tale Riders."

xref.title: Asteroid Named After Him
xref.body: An asteroid has been officially named after Brian May, a significant honor recognizing his scientific contributions. "Oh, yeah, and there's an asteroid named after him."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Astrophysicist and Academic Chancellor
xref.body: Brian May is a distinguished physicist with a doctorate earned for his work titled "A Survey of Radio Velocities in the Zodiacal Dust Cloud." He currently holds the prestigious position of chancellor at Liverpool University, succeeding Cherie Blair (Tony Blair's wife) in this role. "He's a full fledged physicist with a doctorate based on his work called a survey of radio velocities in the zodiacal dust cloud."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Brian May as Primary Influence
xref.body: Adam Slack considers Brian May of Queen his greatest influence, even commissioning a custom KZ Guitar Works instrument that was directly inspired by one of Brian May's guitars. "If you had to ask Adam about his greatest influence, he would probably tell you it was Brian May of Queen."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Brian May's Astrophysics Doctorate
xref.body: Queen guitarist Brian May is a full-fledged astrophysicist, holding a PhD. His doctoral thesis, titled "A Survey of Radio Velocities in the Zodiacal Dust Cloud," spans 256 pages. "Brian May is a full-blown astrophysicist. His PhD was entitled A Survey of Radio Velocities in the Zodiacal Dust Cloud."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Collaborator on Dennis Wilson's "Holy Man"
xref.body: Roger Taylor contributed to the completion of Dennis Wilson's unfinished song "Holy Man," working alongside Taylor Hawkins and Brian May. This collaboration highlights his respect for and connection with Hawkins. "Taylor added to music, wrote some new lyrics, sang the song, and he was backed up by Roger Taylor and Brian May."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: First Guitar Hero
xref.body: Tom York's earliest guitar hero was Brian May of Queen, whose guitar solo in "Bohemian Rhapsody" he still admires. "And his first guitar hero, it was Brian May of Queen."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Major Influence on Adam Slack
xref.body: Queen, and specifically guitarist Brian May, were a major influence on Adam Slack of The Struts, inspiring his playing style and even custom guitar designs. "If you had to ask Adam about his greatest influence, he would probably tell you it was Brian May of Queen."

xref.title: Taylor Hawkins' Lead Vocals
xref.body: Taylor Hawkins was the only member other than Dave Grohl to sing lead on Foo Fighters songs. He sang on covers like Pink Floyd's "Have a Cigar" (with Brian May on guitar), Cream's "I Feel Fine," and Joe Walsh's "Life of Illusion," as well as original songs like "Cold Day in the Sun" and "Sunday Rain." "Just to show you how special a place Taylor Hawkins had within the food fighters, he is the only guy other than Dave Grohl to sing lead on a food song."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
